name: Shot Types
entries: close view: the main subjects fill most of the frame, with the contact points and details needed to understand their action still visible
middle view: the main subjects from their middle up, widening or lowering the frame when their hands, supports or lower-body action must be visible
full view: every main subject whole in the frame, from its top to where it rests on the ground, with space around it
distant view: the main subjects small within a wide place, the surroundings filling most of the frame
shared close view: the main subjects' faces and interacting hands share the frame, with enough surrounding context to distinguish who does what
knee-up view: the main subjects are shown from above their heads to below their knees, retaining the spacing between their bodies
environmental view: the main subjects occupy a readable part of the frame while the surrounding workspace or terrain explains the activity
wide horizontal view: the frame extends to either side of the main subjects, keeping their lateral relationships and the nearby space visible
